blocks.source: Canto XIII
blocks.translation: Canto XIII

blocks.source: Non era ancor di là Nesso arrivato,
blocks.translation: Not yet had Nessus reached the other side,

blocks.source: quando noi ci mettemmo per un bosco
blocks.translation: When we had put ourselves within a wood,

blocks.source: che da neun sentiero era segnato.
blocks.translation: That was not marked by any path whatever.

blocks.source: Non fronda verde, ma di color fosco;
blocks.translation: Not foliage green, but of a dusky colour,

blocks.source: non rami schietti, ma nodosi e ’nvolti;
blocks.translation: Not branches smooth, but gnarled and intertangled,

blocks.source: non pomi v’eran, ma stecchi con tòsco.
blocks.translation: No fruits were there, but thorns with poison.

blocks.source: Non han sì aspri sterpi né sì folti
blocks.translation: Such tangled thickets have not, nor so dense,

blocks.source: quelle fiere selvagge che ’n odio hanno
blocks.translation: Those savage wild beasts, that in hatred hold

blocks.source: tra Cecina e Corneto i luoghi cólti.
blocks.translation: ’Twixt Cecina and Corneto the tilled places.

blocks.source: Quivi le brutte Arpie lor nidi fanno,
blocks.translation: There do the hideous Harpies make their nests,

blocks.source: che cacciar de le Strofade i Troiani
blocks.translation: Who chased the Trojans from the Strophades,

blocks.source: con tristo annunzio di futuro danno.
blocks.translation: With sad announcement of impending doom;

blocks.source: Ali hanno late, e colli e visi umani,
blocks.translation: Broad wings have they, and necks and faces human,

blocks.source: piè con artigli, e pennuto ’l gran ventre;
blocks.translation: And feet with claws, and their great bellies fledged;

blocks.source: fanno lamenti in su li alberi strani.
blocks.translation: They make laments upon the wondrous trees.

blocks.source: E ’l buon maestro «Prima che più entre,
blocks.translation: And the good Master: “Ere thou enter farther,

blocks.source: sappi che se’ nel secondo girone»,
blocks.translation: Know that thou art within the second round,”

blocks.source: mi cominciò a dire, «e sarai mentre
blocks.translation: Thus he began to say, “and shalt be, till

blocks.source: che tu verrai ne l’orribil sabbione.
blocks.translation: Thou comest out upon the horrible sand;

blocks.source: Però riguarda ben; sì vederai
blocks.translation: Therefore look well around, and thou shalt see

blocks.source: cose che torrien fede al mio sermone».
blocks.translation: Things that would rob my words of all belief.”

blocks.source: Io sentia d’ogne parte trarre guai
blocks.translation: I heard on all sides lamentations uttered,

blocks.source: e non vedea persona che ’l facesse;
blocks.translation: And person none beheld I who might make them,

blocks.source: per ch’io tutto smarrito m’arrestai.
blocks.translation: Whence, utterly bewildered, I stood still.

blocks.source: Cred’ ïo ch’ei credette ch’io credesse
blocks.translation: I think he thought that I perhaps might think

blocks.source: che tante voci uscisser, tra quei bronchi,
blocks.translation: So many voices issued through those trunks

blocks.source: da gente che per noi si nascondesse.
blocks.translation: From people who concealed themselves from us;

blocks.source: Però disse ’l maestro: «Se tu tronchi
blocks.translation: Therefore the Master said: “If thou break off

blocks.source: qualche fraschetta d’una d’este piante,
blocks.translation: Some little spray from any of these trees,

blocks.source: li pensier c’hai si faran tutti monchi».
blocks.translation: The thoughts thou hast will wholly be made vain.”

blocks.source: Allor porsi la mano un poco avante
blocks.translation: Then stretched I forth my hand a little forward,

blocks.source: e colsi un ramicel da un gran pruno;
blocks.translation: And plucked a branchlet off from a great thorn;

blocks.source: e ’l tronco suo gridò: «Perché mi schiante?».
blocks.translation: And the trunk cried, “Why dost thou mangle me?”

blocks.source: Da che fatto fu poi di sangue bruno,
blocks.translation: After it had become embrowned with blood,

blocks.source: ricominciò a dir: «Perché mi scerpi?
blocks.translation: It recommenced its cry: “Why dost thou rend me?

blocks.source: non hai tu spirto di pietade alcuno?
blocks.translation: Hast thou no spirit of pity whatsoever?

blocks.source: Uomini fummo, e or siam fatti sterpi:
blocks.translation: Men once we were, and now are changed to trees;

blocks.source: ben dovrebb’ esser la tua man più pia,
blocks.translation: Indeed, thy hand should be more pitiful,

blocks.source: se state fossimo anime di serpi».
blocks.translation: Even if the souls of serpents we had been.”

blocks.source: Come d’un stizzo verde ch’arso sia
blocks.translation: As out of a green brand, that is on fire

blocks.source: da l’un de’ capi, che da l’altro geme
blocks.translation: At one of the ends, and from the other drips

blocks.source: e cigola per vento che va via,
blocks.translation: And hisses with the wind that is escaping;

blocks.source: sì de la scheggia rotta usciva insieme
blocks.translation: So from that splinter issued forth together

blocks.source: parole e sangue; ond’ io lasciai la cima
blocks.translation: Both words and blood; whereat I let the tip

blocks.source: cadere, e stetti come l’uom che teme.
blocks.translation: Fall, and stood like a man who is afraid.

blocks.source: «S’elli avesse potuto creder prima»,
blocks.translation: “Had he been able sooner to believe,”

blocks.source: rispuose ’l savio mio, «anima lesa,
blocks.translation: My Sage made answer, “O thou wounded soul,

blocks.source: ciò c’ha veduto pur con la mia rima,
blocks.translation: What he had seen but in my verses,

blocks.source: non averebbe in te la man distesa;
blocks.translation: Not upon thee had he stretched forth his hand;

blocks.source: ma la cosa incredibile mi fece
blocks.translation: Whereas the thing incredible has caused me

blocks.source: indurlo ad ovra ch’a me stesso pesa.
blocks.translation: To put him to an act which grieveth me.

blocks.source: Ma dilli chi tu fosti, sì che ’n vece
blocks.translation: But tell him who thou wast, so that by way

blocks.source: d’alcun’ ammenda tua fama rinfreschi
blocks.translation: Of some amends thy fame he may refresh

blocks.source: nel mondo sù, dove tornar li lece».
blocks.translation: Up in the world, to which he can return.”

blocks.source: E ’l tronco: «Sì col dolce dir m’adeschi,
blocks.translation: And the trunk said: “So thy sweet words allure me,

blocks.source: ch’i’ non posso tacere; e voi non gravi
blocks.translation: I cannot silent be; and you be vexed not,

blocks.source: perch’ ïo un poco a ragionar m’inveschi.
blocks.translation: That I a little to discourse am tempted.

blocks.source: Io son colui che tenni ambo le chiavi
blocks.translation: I am the one who both keys had in keeping

blocks.source: del cor di Federigo, e che le volsi,
blocks.translation: Of Frederick’s heart, and turned them to and fro

blocks.source: serrando e diserrando, sì soavi,
blocks.translation: So softly in unlocking and in locking,

blocks.source: che dal secreto suo quasi ogn’ uom tolsi;
blocks.translation: That from his secrets most men I withheld;

blocks.source: fede portai al glorïoso offizio,
blocks.translation: Fidelity I bore the glorious office

blocks.source: tanto ch’i’ ne perde’ li sonni e ’ polsi.
blocks.translation: So great, I lost thereby my sleep and pulses.

blocks.source: La meretrice che mai da l’ospizio
blocks.translation: The courtesan who never from the dwelling

blocks.source: di Cesare non torse li occhi putti,
blocks.translation: Of Caesar turned aside her strumpet eyes,

blocks.source: morte comune e de le corti vizio,
blocks.translation: Death universal and the vice of courts,

blocks.source: infiammò contra me li animi tutti;
blocks.translation: Inflamed against me all the other minds,

blocks.source: e li ’nfiammati infiammar sì Augusto,
blocks.translation: And they, inflamed, did so inflame Augustus,

blocks.source: che ’ lieti onor tornaro in tristi lutti.
blocks.translation: That my glad honours turned to dismal mournings.

blocks.source: L’animo mio, per disdegnoso gusto,
blocks.translation: My spirit, moved by bitterness of scorn,

blocks.source: credendo col morir fuggir disdegno,
blocks.translation: Thinking by dying to escape disdain,

blocks.source: ingiusto fece me contra me giusto.
blocks.translation: Made me unjust against myself, the just.

blocks.source: Per le nove radici d’esto legno
blocks.translation: I, by the roots unwonted of this wood,

blocks.source: vi giuro che già mai non ruppi fede
blocks.translation: Do swear to you that never broke I faith

blocks.source: al mio segnor, che fu d’onor sì degno.
blocks.translation: Unto my lord, who was so worthy of honour;

blocks.source: E se di voi alcun nel mondo riede,
blocks.translation: And to the world if one of you return,

blocks.source: conforti la memoria mia, che giace
blocks.translation: Let him my memory comfort, which is lying

blocks.source: ancor del colpo che ’nvidia le diede».
blocks.translation: Still prostrate from the blow that envy dealt it.”

blocks.source: Un poco attese, e poi «Da ch’el si tace»,
blocks.translation: Waited awhile, and then: “Since he is silent,”

blocks.source: disse ’l poeta a me, «non perder l’ora;
blocks.translation: The Poet said to me, “lose not the time,

blocks.source: ma parla, e chiedi a lui, se più ti piace».
blocks.translation: But speak, and question him, if more may please thee.”

blocks.source: Ond’ ïo a lui: «Domandal tu ancora
blocks.translation: Whence I to him: “Do thou again inquire

blocks.source: di quel che credi ch’a me satisfaccia;
blocks.translation: Concerning what thou thinks’t will satisfy me;

blocks.source: ch’i’ non potrei, tanta pietà m’accora».
blocks.translation: For I cannot, such pity is in my heart.”

blocks.source: Perciò ricominciò: «Se l’om ti faccia
blocks.translation: Therefore he recommenced: “So may the man

blocks.source: liberamente ciò che ’l tuo dir priega,
blocks.translation: Do for thee freely what thy speech implores,

blocks.source: spirito incarcerato, ancor ti piaccia
blocks.translation: Spirit incarcerate, again be pleased

blocks.source: di dirne come l’anima si lega
blocks.translation: To tell us in what way the soul is bound

blocks.source: in questi nocchi; e dinne, se tu puoi,
blocks.translation: Within these knots; and tell us, if thou canst,

blocks.source: s’alcuna mai di tai membra si spiega».
blocks.translation: If any from such members e’er is freed.”

blocks.source: Allor soffiò il tronco forte, e poi
blocks.translation: Then blew the trunk amain, and afterward

blocks.source: si convertì quel vento in cotal voce:
blocks.translation: The wind was into such a voice converted:

blocks.source: «Brievemente sarà risposto a voi.
blocks.translation: “With brevity shall be replied to you.

blocks.source: Quando si parte l’anima feroce
blocks.translation: When the exasperated soul abandons

blocks.source: dal corpo ond’ ella stessa s’è disvelta,
blocks.translation: The body whence it rent itself away,

blocks.source: Minòs la manda a la settima foce.
blocks.translation: Minos consigns it to the seventh abyss.

blocks.source: Cade in la selva, e non l’è parte scelta;
blocks.translation: It falls into the forest, and no part

blocks.source: ma là dove fortuna la balestra,
blocks.translation: Is chosen for it; but where Fortune hurls it,

blocks.source: quivi germoglia come gran di spelta.
blocks.translation: There like a grain of spelt it germinates.

blocks.source: Surge in vermena e in pianta silvestra:
blocks.translation: It springs a sapling, and a forest tree;

blocks.source: l’Arpie, pascendo poi de le sue foglie,
blocks.translation: The Harpies, feeding then upon its leaves,

blocks.source: fanno dolore, e al dolor fenestra.
blocks.translation: Do pain create, and for the pain an outlet.

blocks.source: Come l’altre verrem per nostre spoglie,
blocks.translation: Like others for our spoils shall we return;

blocks.source: ma non però ch’alcuna sen rivesta,
blocks.translation: But not that any one may them revest,

blocks.source: ché non è giusto aver ciò ch’om si toglie.
blocks.translation: For ’tis not just to have what one casts off.

blocks.source: Qui le strascineremo, e per la mesta
blocks.translation: Here we shall drag them, and along the dismal

blocks.source: selva saranno i nostri corpi appesi,
blocks.translation: Forest our bodies shall suspended be,

blocks.source: ciascuno al prun de l’ombra sua molesta».
blocks.translation: Each to the thorn of his molested shade.”

blocks.source: Noi eravamo ancora al tronco attesi,
blocks.translation: We were attentive still unto the trunk,

blocks.source: credendo ch’altro ne volesse dire,
blocks.translation: Thinking that more it yet might wish to tell us,

blocks.source: quando noi fummo d’un romor sorpresi,
blocks.translation: When by a tumult we were overtaken,

blocks.source: similemente a colui che venire
blocks.translation: In the same way as he is who perceives

blocks.source: sente ’l porco e la caccia a la sua posta,
blocks.translation: The boar and chase approaching to his stand,

blocks.source: ch’ode le bestie, e le frasche stormire.
blocks.translation: Who hears the crashing of the beasts and branches;

blocks.source: Ed ecco due da la sinistra costa,
blocks.translation: And two behold! upon our left-hand side,

blocks.source: nudi e graffiati, fuggendo sì forte,
blocks.translation: Naked and scratched, fleeing so furiously,

blocks.source: che de la selva rompieno ogne rosta.
blocks.translation: That every branch that barred their way they broke.

blocks.source: Quel dinanzi: «Or accorri, accorri, morte!».
blocks.translation: He who was in advance: “Now help, Death, help!”

blocks.source: E l’altro, cui pareva tardar troppo,
blocks.translation: And the other one, who seemed to lag too much,

blocks.source: gridava: «Lano, sì non furo accorte
blocks.translation: Was shouting: “Lano, were not so alert

blocks.source: le gambe tue a le giostre dal Toppo!».
blocks.translation: Those legs of thine at joustings of the Toppo!”

blocks.source: E poi che forse li fallia la lena,
blocks.translation: And then, perchance because his breath was failing,

blocks.source: di sé e d’un cespuglio fece un groppo.
blocks.translation: He grouped himself together with a bush.

blocks.source: Di rietro a loro era la selva piena
blocks.translation: Behind them was the forest full of black

blocks.source: di nere cagne, bramose e correnti
blocks.translation: She-mastiffs, ravenous, and swift of foot

blocks.source: come veltri ch’uscisser di catena.
blocks.translation: As greyhounds, who are issuing from the chain.

blocks.source: In quel che s’appiattò miser li denti,
blocks.translation: On him who had crouched down they set their teeth,

blocks.source: e quel dilaceraro a brano a brano;
blocks.translation: And him they lacerated piece by piece,

blocks.source: poi sen portar quelle membra dolenti.
blocks.translation: Thereafter bore away those aching members.

blocks.source: Presemi allor la mia scorta per mano,
blocks.translation: Thereat my Escort took me by the hand,

blocks.source: e menommi al cespuglio che piangea
blocks.translation: And led me to the bush, that all in vain

blocks.source: per le rotture sanguinenti in vano.
blocks.translation: Was weeping from its bloody lacerations.

blocks.source: «O Iacopo», dicea, «da Santo Andrea,
blocks.translation: “O Jacopo,” it said, “of Sant’ Andrea,

blocks.source: che t’è giovato di me fare schermo?
blocks.translation: What helped it thee of me to make a screen?

blocks.source: che colpa ho io de la tua vita rea?».
blocks.translation: What blame have I in thy nefarious life?”

blocks.source: Quando ’l maestro fu sovr’ esso fermo,
blocks.translation: When near him had the Master stayed his steps,

blocks.source: disse: «Chi fosti, che per tante punte
blocks.translation: He said: “Who wast thou, that through wounds so many

blocks.source: soffi con sangue doloroso sermo?».
blocks.translation: Art blowing out with blood thy dolorous speech?”

blocks.source: Ed elli a noi: «O anime che giunte
blocks.translation: And he to us: “O souls, that hither come

blocks.source: siete a veder lo strazio disonesto
blocks.translation: To look upon the shameful massacre

blocks.source: c’ha le mie fronde sì da me disgiunte,
blocks.translation: That has so rent away from me my leaves,

blocks.source: raccoglietele al piè del tristo cesto.
blocks.translation: Gather them up beneath the dismal bush;

blocks.source: I’ fui de la città che nel Batista
blocks.translation: I of that city was which to the Baptist

blocks.source: mutò ’l primo padrone; ond’ ei per questo
blocks.translation: Changed its first patron, wherefore he for this

blocks.source: sempre con l’arte sua la farà trista;
blocks.translation: Forever with his art will make it sad.

blocks.source: e se non fosse che ’n sul passo d’Arno
blocks.translation: And were it not that on the pass of Arno

blocks.source: rimane ancor di lui alcuna vista,
blocks.translation: Some glimpses of him are remaining still,

blocks.source: que’ cittadin che poi la rifondarno
blocks.translation: Those citizens, who afterwards rebuilt it

blocks.source: sovra ’l cener che d’Attila rimase,
blocks.translation: Upon the ashes left by Attila,

blocks.source: avrebber fatto lavorare indarno.
blocks.translation: In vain had caused their labour to be done.

blocks.source: Io fei gibetto a me de le mie case».
blocks.translation: Of my own house I made myself a gibbet.”
